blocks.title: Toxicity
blocks.text: Toxicity is the extent to which a substance can harm an organism or the environment.
A material may be toxic during its production, its use and its final disposal. Toxicity is measured by the extent and type of hazard that a material may cause, and there are several types of hazard.

items: Health hazards: a substance damages health on exposure. Chromium compounds, for example, are carcinogens (cause cancer) and mutagens (change DNA and genes) and cause respiratory problems; some additives in plastics can cause hormonal problems.

Physical hazards: harm due to physical or chemical properties, to buildings, humans, ecosystems and the environment; for example a flammable or explosive material can harm people and forests or damage a building.

Environmental hazards: long-term harm to aquatic life or the environment. Heavy metals such as lead, mercury and cadmium can leach into soil and groundwater and are dangerous to plants, land animals, fish and other aquatic organisms.

blocks.alt: Top: three boxes for health hazards (chromium a carcinogen and mutagen; plastic additives affect hormones), physical hazards (flammable or explosive materials) and environmental hazards (Pb, Hg, Cd leaching into soil). Bottom: a chain of five boxes joined by arrows: electronics, batteries and fluorescent lights; discarded as waste; leach into soil and groundwater; taken up by plants, fish and other organisms; reach humans through food and water.
blocks.caption: Kinds of hazard and the path of heavy metals (original diagram for topics 31.2.1 and 31.2.2).
blocks.long_description: Heavy metals thrown away in electronic waste do not disappear. They leach into soil and water, pass into living things and move up the food chain to humans.

blocks.prompt: What is the difference between a health hazard and an environmental hazard?
blocks.explanation: A health hazard damages a person's health on exposure (e.g. chromium causing cancer); an environmental hazard causes long-term harm to aquatic life or the environment (e.g. heavy metals leaching into soil).

items: Toxicity: how far a substance can harm organisms or the environment.
